test_title: PYST 15: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - Mathematics (Held On: 13 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: Anjani can do a certain piece of work in 24 days. Anjani and Khushbu can together do the same work in 20 days, and Anjani, Khushbu and Sushmita can do the same work together in 8 days. In how many days can Anjani and Sushmita do the same work?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM of days (24, 20, 8) = 120 units.

Efficiency of A = 120 ÷ 24 = 5 units/day.

Efficiency of (A + K) = 120 ÷ 20 = 6 units/day, and (A + K + S) = 120 ÷ 8 = 15 units/day.

Efficiency of S = 15 − 6 = 9 units/day.

Time taken by A and S together = Total work ÷ Combined Efficiency = 120 ÷ (5 + 9) = 120 ÷ 14 = 60/7 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 60/7 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Anjani (A) = 24 days

Time taken by Anjani and Khushbu (A + K) = 20 days

Time taken by Anjani, Khushbu, and Sushmita (A + K + S) = 8 days

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Anjani (A)
 24
 120
 120 ÷ 24 = 5
 
 

 Anjani + Khushbu (A + K)
 20
 120 ÷ 20 = 6
 
 

 Anjani + Khushbu + Sushmita (A + K + S)
 8
 120 ÷ 8 = 15
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of Sushmita (S) = Combined Efficiency of (A + K + S) − Combined Efficiency of (A + K)

⇒ Efficiency of S = 15 − 6 = 9 units/day

⇒ Combined Efficiency of Anjani and Sushmita (A + S) = Efficiency of A + Efficiency of S

⇒ Combined Efficiency of (A + S) = 5 + 9 = 14 units/day

⇒ Time taken by A and S together = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency of (A + S)

⇒ Time taken = 120 ÷ 14 = 60/7 days

**∴ The correct answer is 60/7 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in proportion to the total work done by each individual. If they work for the same number of days, wages are distributed exactly in the ratio of their daily efficiencies.

Pipes and Cisterns

Follows the same logic as time and work concepts. A pipe filling a tank has a positive efficiency, while a leak or an emptying pipe has a negative efficiency. Net work equals the sum of these respective efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

When individuals work on alternate days, calculate the total work completed in one full cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 people). Then find the total number of full cycles needed to reach closest to the total work.
